title: The Journey That Started Something
description: I travelled all the way from Kerala to Bangalore just to prove that I could. It wasn't meant to be about love, but somehow that little ego-driven journey became the moment that set everything else in motion.

title: The Night I Told You
description: The full-night bike ride, the warmth of the night, and the moment I finally confessed my love to you.

title: Thattekad — Mini Switzerland
description: A cool morning at Thattekad. The atmosphere was calm, the grounds felt almost unreal, and we spent the morning being playful together.

title: Four Hours Close
description: Our first time cuddling. We were together for about four hours. But what stayed with me wasn't simply the closeness. My love for you was sincere. It was about you, not just the moment.

title: The First Goodbye
description: I followed your bus all the way to Perumbavoor, just to steal another twenty minutes with you. But when the time came for you to leave, I felt as though something inside me was quietly falling apart. I stood there anyway, watching you for those final few minutes, trying to hold on to the little time we had left before we had to be apart again.

title: The Day I Fell a Little Deeper
description:
Almost a month had passed since the first visit that made me fall for you, and nearly a week had gone by since you left for Bengaluru. This time, I was there to see you again.

The day was filled with little moments that, on their own, might have seemed ordinary. We sat together on a bench in front of an apartment until a man asked us to leave. We visited Cubbon Park together as a couple for the first time, shared an incredibly hot and spicy chicken fried rice for lunch, and I even fed you a few bites.

Cubbon Park gave me a little “protein” of its own, too—a memory I'll leave here in our own words. And, as usual, you entrusted me with your little belongings: your lip balm, college ID and neck chain. Before leaving, I checked all my pockets and returned your lip balm and ID, both of which we had nearly forgotten about. Your neck chain, however, remained tucked inside my shirt pocket. I didn't realise it was still there until I reached the Kodegehalli Gate bus stop.

But the moments that stayed with me most were much simpler. Whenever we crossed the busy roads, you held my hand and pulled me along beside you, looking after me in that familiar, almost instinctive way. It reminded me of how someone might guide a little brother or a child safely across the road. You may not have thought much of it, but those little gestures stayed with me throughout the day. Somewhere between one crossing and the next, I found myself falling for you a little deeper.

When it was finally time to return home, I left with a strange mixture of happiness and sadness. I was grateful for every moment we'd shared, yet already wished I could have stayed a little longer.

title: A Little Further, Just to Be With You
description:
It was the day you were returning, and for the first time, I accompanied you and your amma to say goodbye. My original plan was to part ways with you at Muvattupuzha, but I followed your bus, hoping it would stop somewhere near Perumbavoor. To my surprise, it continued right through Perumbavoor and all the way to the Indian Oil Swagath petrol pump in Angamaly.

That unexpected detour gave us a little more time together. We had ice cream, teased each other, and even had a small disagreement about Kevin. Among all these little moments, one stood out in particular: a group of schoolgirls called out “Couples corner!” from their bus. It was such an unexpected, amusing moment that it became one of the day's most vivid memories.

Before we parted, I received one last, warm hug from you. It was a small moment, but one I carried with me on the journey home.

By the time I reached Pandappilly at around 11:30 PM, my bike had travelled approximately 99 kilometres. What had begun as a simple goodbye at Muvattupuzha had turned into a much longer journey, all because I wanted a little more time with you.

title: The Two Days That Felt Like a Lifetime
description:
• Day One — 10 October

It was my third visit to Bengaluru, and once again, I was there to see you. I waited at Aster Hospital until around 10:50 AM while you finished your exam. Afterwards, we walked to Theertha, hoping to have biriyani. You told me you weren't particularly hungry, but you still wanted me to eat something. I loved that little gesture; even when you didn't feel like eating yourself, you were thinking about me.

When we reached Theertha, we were told that the biriyani would only be ready by 1:30 PM. So we went upstairs for ice cream. Just as we were there, a group of your friends arrived. I was nervous, although I tried my best to stay calm. One of them even asked my name and whether I had come all the way from Kerala just to meet you. All I could manage was an awkward smile.

After our ice cream, we returned downstairs and waited for the biriyani. The chechi at the restaurant would occasionally look over at us with a gentle smile. By the time our food arrived, even the wait had become part of the memory.

We ate and headed to Sahakara Nagar Park, where we spent time sharing our music with each other. Later, we visited Vishal Mega Mart, where we accidentally broke a bag on display, and bought two packets of soan papdi and some Dairy Milk. We then spent some time at the park near Periyar Cafe before I dropped you in front of your hostel.

But the day wasn't quite over.

Around 9 PM, after you'd had dinner, I asked whether I could charge my phone inside your hostel. I handed it to you, and we talked until midnight, with the iron grill between us—you inside the hostel and me outside. Even that barrier couldn't stop us from finding a little more time together. There was another one of our private “protein” moments through the bars, and by the time we said goodnight, my phone had charged too.

Then came my first real taste of Bengaluru's nights: barking dogs, relentless mosquitoes, and very little comfort. It was hardly the peaceful night I'd imagined, but I was still excited about what the morning would bring.

• Day Two — 11 October

I woke up around 3:30 AM, already excited to see you again. With so much energy and anticipation, I found myself stretching and jumping around the street while waiting for the hostel gate to open. You finally came out around 5:45 AM. During the wait, you'd given me my bag, and I changed my clothes outside the hostel—right in front of its security camera. Looking back, even that became another funny detail from our time together.

We walked towards Aster, where I brushed my teeth and freshened up before we had a good coffee. Then you suggested that we go to Madiwala for breakfast at a Kerala restaurant. We took the buses there and had appam with chicken stew. I enjoyed the meal, and seeing how much you liked it made it even better.

After breakfast, we returned to Cubbon Park and wandered around, looking for a quiet place where we could sit together. Eventually, we found somewhere to settle down and spend some time with each other.

Unfortunately, my stomach began to ache, while you were struggling with a terrible headache and leg pain. You became upset, feeling that I wasn't paying enough attention to you. I struggled to show you how much I cared because I was caught up in my own discomfort. It was a difficult moment between us, and I wished I'd been better at making you feel cared for even when I wasn't feeling well myself.

We returned to Theertha for biriyani, and by then, the people at the restaurant recognised us. After eating, we felt much more like our usual, lively selves again.

Later, we went back to Sahakara Nagar Park and sat together on a bench. That was when you began sharing your family stories with me. As you spoke about your mother, your eyes filled with tears, and I held you close while you cried. I wanted you to feel safe enough to let everything out, without having to hide what you were feeling or worry about being judged.

That moment stayed with me more deeply than anything else that day. Being trusted with your vulnerable side made me feel that I could be someone you leaned on—not someone who needed you to be happy all the time, but someone who could sit beside you when things hurt. I felt closer to you, and I found myself falling for you even more.

When we finally left the park, we bought cotton candy, and you fed me some as we walked back towards your hostel. You also gave me another familiar scolding for not eating properly. Some things, apparently, never change.

Before we parted, you gave me a warm kiss on my hand. I then began the walk to Kodegehalli Gate, carrying two days' worth of memories with me. This time, there was no need to rush. I had plenty of time before my train, so I let my thoughts wander back through everything we'd shared.

I reached KR Puram and boarded my train around 11:50 PM. The journey brought me back to Aluva at approximately 11:20 AM the following morning, and I reached home around 2:15 PM.

We took no photographs during those two days. Yet, somehow, they left me with one of the fullest collections of memories I could have asked for. From shared meals and silly accidents to sleepless nights, difficult moments, and the trust you placed in me, every part of the visit gave me something to carry home.

And with every journey I make to see you, my love for you grows a little stronger.

title: One Hour, A Thousand Feelings
description:
That day, I found myself wandering through Pandappilly town several times, hoping for a chance to see you. My repeated trips didn't go unnoticed, and they made your amma suspect that I wanted to meet you. She told you that if I wanted to come over and talk to you, I could do so when she was home.

At around 8:20 PM, amma asked whether I was coming. And just like that, I got the chance I'd been hoping for. I walked into your house, happier than I could explain, simply because I finally got to see you up close.

We talked about random things, and somehow, the arguments we'd had throughout the day no longer felt so important. Being together in person softened everything. I also got to have a conversation with your amma, which made the visit feel even more special.

Then, while your amma and brother were occupied with a phone call, I managed to steal a hug. I didn't feel like letting go. What followed was a little push-and-pull between us, and in the middle of it, I accidentally broke your phone. The most unexpected part was that your brother seemed to understand exactly what had happened.

Despite that little accident, I left the house at 9:23 PM with a heart full of happiness. From the moment I arrived to the moment I left, we had shared just over an hour together. It wasn't a long visit, but it was enough to melt away the day's arguments and leave me with another memory I wanted to keep.

title: Together, Like We Were Already Home
description:
Day 1 — October 21: A Journey That Almost Went Wrong

It all started with a conversation about travelling together. We both wanted to spend time with each other, away from our usual routines, so we planned a trip to Bangalore.

Our original plan was to reach Bangalore on the morning of October 22, spend the entire day exploring the city, and perhaps experience its nightlife together. Her classes were initially announced to begin on Friday, October 23, so she managed to convince her mother to let her leave home on Wednesday, October 21.

But sometimes, even the simplest plans can become complicated.

With both of us occupied with our own schedules, we misunderstood each other's train plans. She had planned to take the Ernakulam Express, while I had planned to take the Kanyakumari Express. I couldn't reach the station in time for her train, and with her mother's strong insistence, she was forced to board the Ernakulam Express without me.

I called her and asked her to get down at the nearest station so that we could continue the journey together. Eventually, she got down at Thrissur, frustrated and in a terrible mood after the crowded journey. I knew she needed something to calm her down, so I bought her favourite Hide & Seek and Bourbon biscuits.

When I boarded the Kanyakumari Express, we spoke again and came up with another plan. Either I would get down at Thrissur and we would take a later train, or she would join me on the Kanyakumari Express. We made a deal: if I managed to find two seats by the time the train reached Thrissur, she would join me. Otherwise, I would get down and figure things out with her.

And somehow, fortune was on our side. Just as the train reached Thrissur, I managed to secure two seats.

It was a close call. Had I not found those seats, she probably would have given me a hard time for a very long while!

Somewhere along the journey, we also discovered that her classes would actually begin on October 22, a day earlier than we had expected. But she firmly decided that she wasn't going to class that morning.

Finally, we were together. We sat beside each other, talked, and settled into the journey. I spent much of the time asleep, while she barely managed to get any proper rest.

It wasn't the smooth beginning we had imagined, but it was our beginning nonetheless.

Day 2 — October 22: A Room, a Lake, and the Little Things

We reached Krishnarajapuram at 6:41 am. She was exhausted because she hadn't slept properly during the journey. We bought a toothbrush and toothpaste for her, freshened up at the station, and made our way towards Central Silk Board by bus.

It was a pleasant bus ride, and soon we were walking towards Kairali Restaurant for breakfast.

Somewhere along the way, we even managed to splash a little water on each other in the washroom. Such a tiny, silly moment, but that was already becoming our thing.

By the time we finished breakfast, she was at her lowest energy level and desperately wanted somewhere to rest her head. So we started searching for a place to stay and eventually found Zolo Hibiscus Hotel.

The check-in time was 1 pm and checkout was at 11 am. We waited around for a while because nobody was available at reception. Eventually, I discovered that the booking had to be completed online. We booked the room and asked whether we could leave our bags there and return at check-in time. Thankfully, they agreed.

And then came one of my brilliant ideas.

I decided to take her to Madiwala Lake Park for a little walk. In my imagination, it would be a pleasant place to spend some time together. In reality, we ended up walking through a disappointing stretch of garbage beside what felt like one of the dirtiest lake views imaginable, only to discover that the park was closed.

The destination was a complete flop. But the journey there became one of those memories I wouldn't trade away.

During the walk, I repeatedly asked her to feed me Hide & Seek biscuits, and she actually did. She later recalled how I reminded her of a little child screaming for chocolates while she felt like his mother, patiently feeding him. I still find that memory adorable.

Eventually, we had to make our way back towards Central Silk Board because buses weren't readily available. We took a bus from the lake area, although we suspected that the conductor had charged us unfairly.

Our little adventure had failed spectacularly as a sightseeing plan, but the two of us walking around together, full of energy and completely absorbed in each other, made it worth remembering.

We returned to the hotel, collected our bags, and finally got into our room at around 1:41 pm. After a pleasant chicken biryani and fresh lime from her favourite Kairali Restaurant, she could finally rest her head properly.

We rested together and cuddled, planning to go out around 8 or 9 pm to explore Bangalore's nightlife. But around 7 pm, she received a video call from her mother. Her mother seemed suspicious, and her mood changed. We decided to drop our plans and stay inside instead.

Later, we took turns showering. I was so lazy about getting into the shower that she had to force me to go first. Then it was her turn.

I hadn't brought a towel, so we ended up sharing the same one.

It was such an ordinary thing, something most people wouldn't even think twice about. Yet, in that moment, I felt deeply affectionate towards her. Being with her had a way of making even the simplest things feel extraordinary.

After her shower, she forced me to get a shave and I did so. After getting the shave done, I noticed the soft, baby-like smell she had often been told about by her friends. I pulled her closer and discovered something I would become completely obsessed with: that particular smell of hers after a shower.

It wasn't a grand romantic moment. There was no special place, no elaborate plan, and no perfect scenery. There was just us, sharing a room and discovering how beautiful ordinary closeness could feel.

Day 3 — October 23: The Morning I Didn't Want to Leave

Around 12:30 am, we started craving something sweet. We decided to order ice cream, and when it arrived, the quantity was smaller than we had expected, but the taste was good. We shared it together.

We even considered going out at midnight for tea. I searched for nearby cafés, but by around 1 am, everything seemed to be out of service. So we abandoned that plan too.

The night was warm, comfortable, and full of little moments that belonged only to us. I would ask her for kisses whenever she wanted me to do something for her, even for the smallest things, like picking up her phone from beside the bed. Somehow, even the most ordinary requests became excuses to be affectionate with each other.

We planned to wake up at 4 am, check out, and head towards KSR. I would take the 6 am train home, while she would take an Uber to her hostel.

But when the alarm rang, neither of us was ready for the morning to begin.

She was too lazy to get up and told me that I could leave first and that she would reach her hostel by Uber later. Perhaps she wanted me to stay longer. Whatever the reason, I knew that I didn't want to leave her behind so early.

So I stayed. I decided to take the later train, the one scheduled for 4:10 pm.

One of my warmest memories from that morning was brushing our teeth together. There were little touches, playful gestures, and mischievous moments when I would turn off the tap just to pull her closer. They were tiny things, but they meant so much to me.

For a moment, I could imagine a future morning with her: waking up beside each other, still half-asleep, brushing our teeth together, getting ready for the day, and beginning another ordinary day as a couple who shared a home.

It was only a glimpse of a future we could imagine, but it felt surprisingly real.

As the morning progressed, we became increasingly affectionate, cuddling for hours and losing track of everything around us. Some moments unfolded more intimately than we had planned, but they remain part of our private story, something I want to remember for the closeness and trust we shared rather than reduce to a label.

By around 11 am, we finally got dressed, exchanging random kisses and hugs while getting ready. We checked out at approximately 11 am, had breakfast, and took a bus from Madiwala towards Majestic before continuing to Kodegehalli Gate.

And then came a moment that stayed with me.

We had been together from around 1:41 pm on October 22 until 11:08 am on October 23 — approximately 21 hours and 27 minutes. It was not even a full day, yet it felt like we had lived through so many little chapters together.

When we reached the area near her hostel, she took the longest possible route on our walk. Along the way, she confessed that she wanted me to stay longer and asked me to leave only on the 8 pm train.

Knowing that she wanted me near her made me feel even more loved. I wanted to stay too, but I had work on Saturday and knew I had to get home.

After leaving her luggage at the hostel, we walked towards Vishal Mega Mart because she wanted to buy a few things. She picked up a water bottle, a pack of two books, and a pack of tissues. Along the way, I continued my mischievous antics, surprising her and making her react in ways that made the shopping trip just as entertaining as everything else.

She even tried to convince me to take the 4 pm train, almost as if she knew that I would keep finding reasons to stay if she let me.

At around 3:26 pm, we shared chicken fried rice. After that, we made our way towards Sahakar Nagar Park, where we bought two different ice cream flavours — tender coconut and strawberry. Unfortunately, both were disappointing.

We entered the park and spent much of our time talking about our crazy cuddles and the intimacy we had shared. We laughed, talked, took some photos together and held on to the remaining hours of our time together.

We left the park at around 5:30 pm and reached her hostel around 6 pm. Before I left, we managed a few more mischievous moments and private affection, including a little surprise that left her stunned and amused.

Eventually, it was time to go.

I walked to the Kodegehalli Gate bus stop, caught a bus at around 7 pm, and reached KSR Railway Station at approximately 7:50 pm.

The return journey was far less comfortable than the journey to Bangalore. Even though I reached the station about 25 minutes before departure, I couldn't find a seat. For much of the journey, until around 1 am, I stood or sat on the floor, tired and uncomfortable.

But even then, my mind kept returning to the time we had spent together.

Day 4 — October 24: The Journey Home

Around 1 am, someone woke me up and told me to take an empty upper berth. I settled there and stayed until around 3 am, when I finally found a place on a lower berth.

I sat there for the rest of the journey until we reached Aluva at approximately 7:50 am.

Even while travelling home, we stayed connected. I was on a call with her until 9:18 am, when she had to end it because her class was beginning.

From Aluva, I took a bus to Muvattupuzha and then another one home, finally reaching home at around 10:45 am.

I took a quick bath and left for work.

Just like that, the trip was over. The room, the shared towel, the late-night ice cream, the silly biscuit-feeding ritual, the morning brushing, the long walks, and all the little kisses were now memories instead of moments I could reach out and experience again.

The trip had not gone according to plan. We missed trains, abandoned sightseeing plans, encountered a closed park, ate disappointing ice creams, and endured an uncomfortable return journey. Financially, too, I came home with very little left.

Yet, when I look back, I don't remember the trip as a failure.

I remember two people trying to find their way to each other despite everything that went wrong. I remember how hard it was to leave when we both wanted more time. And I remember how naturally we slipped into sharing the little routines of everyday life.

Perhaps that is what made this trip so special. We didn't need a perfect holiday to imagine a future together.

For a little over twenty-one hours, we got a glimpse of what it might feel like to be together like husband and wife — not because everything was perfect, but because even the ordinary moments felt like home.

title: A complete night for you
description: We spent almost an entire night talking on phone. It was continuously from about 7:14pm to 3:49Am till she fell asleep.
